d.note: Pine Plains tavern building from 1782, restored in the 1990s and run since 2022 by chef-proprietor Clare de Boer, with an upstairs ballroom for events and cooking classes.
d.jbf: Best New Restaurant semifinalist 2023; Best Chef: New York State semifinalist 2024 (Clare de Boer); Best Chef: New York State semifinalist 2025 (Clare de Boer)
d.fn: Its site says the building went up in 1782 as a tavern with rooms and a domed ballroom; it declined after World War I and reopened as a restaurant in 1995

d.note: Family-run village bagel shop for breakfast and lunch, eat-in or takeout.
d.fn: Its site says it has been family owned and operated in the village since 1995; same storefront throughout not confirmed

d.note: Colonial-era tavern inside the Beekman Arms inn at Rhinebeck's main crossroads, serving lunch, brunch and dinner every day of the year.
d.fn: Wikipedia says the tavern (begun 1704 by William Traphagen) moved to this crossroads in 1766; the inn claims to be America's oldest continuously operated inn, and the Village marked its 260th anniversary in July 2026

d.note: Riverfront inn at the foot of Cold Spring's Main Street with two dining rooms (the River Room and the Half Moon Tavern) serving lunch, dinner and Sunday brunch.
d.fn: Its site says the building dates to 1827 and has welcomed guests since 1832, and calls it the second-oldest continuously operated inn in New York State (a claim)

d.note: Rustic-style 1915 park inn run by the Palisades Interstate Park Commission, with a full-service restaurant and bar and seasonal festivals.
d.fn: Built and opened in 1915 inside Bear Mountain State Park (on the National Register); it was closed for renovation about 2006-2012, per Wikipedia

d.note: Rockland bagel shop and deli on Route 59 known for hand-rolled, boiled and baked bagels served hot from the oven.
Nanuet shop of the Rockland bagel café, which hand-rolls, boils and bakes its bagels from dough made on site.
d.fn: Its site says the family's bagel business started in Nyack in 1990. This shop's opening year isn't stated.

d.jbf: Best Chef: New York State semifinalist 2023 (Paolo Garcia Mendoza)

d.note: Rockland bagel café that mixes its dough on site and hand-rolls, boils and bakes its bagels throughout the day. A second shop is in Nanuet.
d.fn: Its site says the family's bagel business started in Nyack in 1990. This shop's opening year isn't stated.

d.note: Colonial-era tavern in Tappan, restored by the Norden family, serving lunch and dinner with live music most nights.
d.fn: Its site says the building dates to 1668 and calls it America's oldest restaurant/tavern (a claim); it figures in the 1780 Major Andre story

d.jbf: Outstanding Restaurateur semifinalist 2023 (Sims and Kirsten Harlow Foster (Foster Supply Hospitality))

d.note: Midtown Kingston shop that ferments sourdough bagels for three days, shapes them by hand, boils them and bakes them on cedar boards.
d.fn: Opened its Kingston shop in November 2024 after starting as a Martha's Vineyard pop-up in 2020

d.note: Historic lakeside mountain resort above New Paltz with a main dining room; day-visit passes include dining options.
d.fn: Its site says the Smiley family founded it in 1869; a National Historic Landmark resort

d.jbf: Best Chef: New York State semifinalist 2024 (Doris Choi)

d.note: Woodstock bakery that hand-rolls, boils and bakes New York-style bagels stuffed with fillings like pizza; now also in Poughkeepsie and Manhattan.
d.fn: The business began in Woodstock in 2021 (idea on New Year's Eve 2020); its site calls Tinker Street the original location

d.note: Small family-run kosher deli, restaurant and caterer on Central Avenue under rabbinic supervision.
d.fn: Its site says the family has cooked the original Epstein's recipes since 1969; year at this address not stated

d.note: Walk-up hot dog stand in a copper-roofed Chinese pagoda on the National Register, splitting and griddling beef-pork-veal dogs; open year-round.
d.fn: Serving hot dogs since 1919; its site says the copper-roofed pagoda stand on Palmer Avenue was built in 1928

d.note: Shrub Oak bagel shop known for its everything bagel. Westfair (Feb 2025) reported about 2,000 bagels on a typical Sunday. Other JV Hot Bagels shops are in Jefferson Valley and Baldwin Place.
Downtown White Plains Cantonese restaurant that specializes in homemade dim sum made fresh every day. Closed Tuesdays. NYSDOH lists it as Aberdeen Cantonese Restaurant.
